header:
Date: 2026-03-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jamie Lin (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (CTO - Castleton), Marcus Holt (Head of Infra), Priya Singh (Lead ML Eng)
Recording: Fireflies.ai auto transcript
Shared links: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/dedicated-overview, security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2
summary: Castleton is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for regulated model inference. Primary drivers: data isolation (no shared pools), predictable throughput for fraud-detection scoring, and burst handling for batch job windows. Key concerns: KMS integration, SSO/SAML, on-prem options vs VPC, GPU sizing and autoscale/burst policy. Next steps are pricing + audit docs, GPU sizing recommendation, and traffic artifacts from customer.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I see Laura, Marcus, Priya - thanks for making time. Well run through your requirements for Dedicated reserved capacity and leave plenty of time for questions.
[00:18] Laura Chen: Thanks Samir, yep excited to kinda get into it. High level we want isolation for our customer data and predictable latency for our fraud scoring models, were looking at reserved GPUs rather than hosted.
[00:30] Jamie Lin: Awesome, to set expectations Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, isolation at the tenant level, options for VPC peering or on-prem if you need air-gap. Also can do burst capacity if you have batch windows.
[00:45] Marcus Holt: Quick question on burst - how does that work? We have nightly batch jobs that spike QPS 4x for 30 minutes. We need to avoid throttling but not pay for peak all month.
[01:00] Jamie Lin: Right, good one. You can configure a committed baseline and a burst pool. Burst can be either pre-provisioned spare hardware on your contract or a cloud-backed burst with automatic fallback to lower-cost models. Theres a policy layer so you can prioritize latency-critical requests.
[01:20] Priya Singh: When you say lower-cost models - do you mean quantized variants? Were sensitive to regression in score delta for fraud model outputs.
[01:32] Samir Patel: Yes - quantized or distilled variants, and we support model pinning. For scoring workloads we usually recommend a small eval suite to measure score drift; Redwoods Optimize recommendations can tune quantization profiles by workload.
[01:50] Speaker 1: (mumble) and can you do KV cash, I mean KV cache for session state?
[01:58] Jamie Lin: Yeah KV cache - sorry transcript hiccup - we manage KV cache across shards, that reduces repeated prefix compute for streaming use cases. For scoring you might use a warm cache for risk-context tokens.
[02:15] Laura Chen: Security - we need KMS with customer keys and audit logs, also SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC.
[02:26] Samir Patel: Absolutely, Dedicated supports KMS integrations (bring-your-own keys), HSM for private deploys, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and detailed audit logs with retention options. We can share SOC2 and ISO reports.
[02:40] Marcus Holt: Any concerns about data residency? We operate in NA and EU regions and need EU data to stay in eu-west-1.
[02:50] Jamie Lin: You can pin capacity to regions, and Dedicated clusters can be deployed into a VPC in the region of choice. For Private on-prem we support an air-gapped option, but thats heavier.
[03:05] Priya Singh: Performance profile: Our scoring model is a 7B decoder, latency SLO is 120 ms 95th for single-call scoring at 512 tokens. Current infra is inference on a single A10G and gets inconsistent p95s during spike.
[03:22] Jamie Lin: For 7B at 512 tokens, we typically run profiling. A10G vs A100 has different kernel choices, and continuous batching can help if you have bursty microbursts. We can propose sizing: baseline concurrency per GPU and autoscale thresholds.
[03:40] Samir Patel: Also worth considering prefix caching if sequences share context, that can cut per-token cost and improve p95.
[03:50] Marcus Holt: How do we validate p99/p95 numbers? Do you run benchmarks with our prompts?
[03:58] Jamie Lin: Yes - pilot runs are common. We can run a lightweight benchmark in your environment or in our dedicated sandbox with your prompt set. Thats part of the POC scope.
[04:12] Laura Chen: Cost is a big factor. If we commit to reserved capacity monthly, what flexibility do we have if usage is lower?
[04:21] Samir Patel: Commitments are tiered. We have minimum reserved months and discounts scale with commit. We also support bursting to on-demand but that might increase unit cost. Recommendation: size for baseline steady traffic and use burst to handle windows, then revisit sizing after 30-60 days based on real telemetry.
[04:40] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) are there preemptible options?
[04:44] Jamie Lin: We do not recommend preemptible for latency-critical scoring. Theres a cheaper variant for non-critical batch scoring.
[04:52] Priya Singh: On networking - can we keep control plane in our VPC? Network egress encrypted, private endpoints?
[04:59] Samir Patel: Yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed VPC peering and private endpoints. For Private deployments the control plane can be either managed with a customer VPC or fully customer-hosted (air-gapped).
[05:15] Marcus Holt: What about compliance artifacts - well need pen test reports and some security questionnaire answers.
[05:22] Samir Patel: Well share our security pack: SOC2 Type II, ISO reports, pen test summary, and an RFP questionnaire template. Ill attach in the follow up.
[05:32] Laura Chen: Any pitfalls customers typically hit during Dedicated onboarding?
[05:36] Jamie Lin: Biggest is underestimating burst patterns and not providing representative prompts; that skews GPU sizing. Also sometimes teams pin to too-large models when a quantized variant would suffice.
[05:50] Speaker 1: (background) latency vs cost tradeoffs are always fun
[05:54] Samir Patel: Yep. We can also do canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies so if a primary model is overloaded we fallback to a compatible variant with slightly different perf/cost characteristics.
[06:10] Priya Singh: For our fraud scoring, false positive rate change of even 0.2% is material. Wed need eval hooks.
[06:18] Jamie Lin: Redwood Optimize supports eval sets and regression alerts; you can tie alerts to rollouts. We recommend a holdout evaluation set and a canary period.
[06:30] Marcus Holt: Are there SLA guarantees for Dedicated? Uptime and latency SLOs?
[06:36] Samir Patel: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on commit tier. We can share the SLA PDF.
[06:45] Laura Chen: On the topic of integration - we run K8s in-house and prefer service-to-service calls. How does your endpoint auth work?
[06:55] Jamie Lin: We support mTLS between your services and Redwood endpoints, token-based auth, and private endpoints inside your VPC.
[07:05] Priya Singh: For experimentation - we'd like a staging cluster. Can that be logically separated but still under the same Dedicated contract?
[07:13] Samir Patel: Yes, you can have multiple clusters under the contract for staging/prod, with different policies and quotas.
[07:21] Laura Chen: Ok can we talk about expected timeline - if we sign a reserved capacity agreement, how long until were live?
[07:28] Jamie Lin: Typical onboarding is 4-6 weeks for a standard Dedicated setup: procurement & legal, KMS/SSO setup, cluster provisioning, and pilot benchmarking. On-prem/private installs take longer (8-12 weeks) due to network and ops coordination.
[07:46] Marcus Holt: For provisioning - do you automate driver/kernel selection or is that manual?
[07:51] Jamie Lin: The runtime selects optimized kernels based on model arch and sequence length; we have a compile/selection pipeline. We do some manual tuning during pilot if needed.
[08:02] Priya Singh: Any recommended GPU type? We were looking at A10G because our cost model favored it.
[08:08] Jamie Lin: A10G is cost-effective for 7B models but A100/RTX gives better p95 headroom. Jamie: well propose a mixed fleet for baseline+burst in the recommendation.
[08:22] Samir Patel: Well also include expected per-token and per-call unit economics in the pricing deck so you can map to your monthly spend.
[08:32] Laura Chen: Great. For the POC scope - we want a short pilot to validate p95/p99 and score drift on our prompts.
[08:40] Samir Patel: Makes sense. Typical pilot: 2 weeks of benchmarking, one week of integration, and then a short rollout. Well define success criteria up front.
[08:50] Marcus Holt: Any runbooks for incident response and escalation?
[08:54] Samir Patel: Yes we provide runbooks and an on-call contact; higher tiers include 24/7 support.
[09:02] Priya Singh: Do you support private key management with our KMS?
[09:07] Samir Patel: Yes BYOK via KMS, HSM supported for Private deployments.
[09:12] Speaker 2: (muffled) how do you handle model rollbacks if a release causes issues?
[09:16] Jamie Lin: Rollbacks are automated via the rollout system, you can set thresholds for auto-fallback, and can do canary steps before full rollout.
[09:26] Laura Chen: Ok that all sounds good. Id like to capture the immediate asks: security pack, pricing, GPU sizing, and a proposed pilot plan.
[09:36] Samir Patel: Noted. Well include a sample pilot statement of work.
[09:40] Priya Singh: One more - do you have latency breakdowns per token and per model call we can reference?
[09:46] Jamie Lin: We have verified perf profiles and per-token breakdowns in the console and can include sample traces from similar customers.
[09:54] Laura Chen: Perfect. Anything else from the team?
[09:58] Marcus Holt: Not from me.
[10:00] Priya Singh: Nope.
[10:02] Samir Patel: Great thanks folks, will follow up with the docs and schedule a technical deep dive with Jamie next week.
[10:09] Laura Chen: Thanks everyone.
[10:12] (call ends)
Notes: transcript contains some auto-transcribe errors (KV cash etc). Recommended follow-up: technical deep dive + pilot SOW.
